meta.source: Cor v2 Supabase (anon REST, build-time read)

thesis: Human systems signal when their conditions are not met, and modern environments withhold those conditions at scale. Preferences are mechanism outputs, not ground truth. The load-bearing claim of every proxy gradient: the cue is identical at every level; only the resolving function changes, so a proxy can fire the cue without supplying what actually resolves it.

foundations.name: Fitness Interface
foundations.statement: Access to the world is mediated by evolved fitness interfaces, not guaranteed veridicality.
foundations.derivation: Hoffman (Interface Theory of Perception), Prakash et al. (Fitness Beats Truth theorem).

foundations.name: Signal-Default Epistemology
foundations.statement: Motivational-emotional outputs are treated as prima facie informative about the organism's regulated conditions, by default. The signal is read as information about input conditions and current state, not as noise to be suppressed. This is a diagnostic default, not a presumption of veridicality (OF1 stands). Reading the signal as information is no argument against relieving it. The default is displaced in two ways. A clear physical defect displaces it outright, whether a test has found it yet or not, and the output is then a symptom of that defect: acute organic disease or state shift (an infection or autoimmune disease, an endocrine disease such as a thyroid fault, delirium), structural damage, a large-effect genetic variant with measurable physical effects, and substance or medication effects. A setting left by deprivation far outside the evolved range (DA7) and chronic dysregulation displace the reading of the current input without making the output a disease: the output answers that setting, or a loop that keeps running, more than the present input. An ordinary hard childhood is no such setting, and even maltreatment, once genes and family are adjusted for, explains little of how an adult feels (DA7). Sleep loss and low-grade inflammation that a mismatched life produces also displace the reading of the current input without making the output a disease. A marker that only shows sensitivity is no defect. Chronic dysregulation counts as a physical cause only where a clear defect is behind it, such as an infection or another separate disease.
foundations.derivation: Frame layer, sibling of OF1. Methodological commitment that follows from P2 + DA1 + DA7: if the architecture is domain-sensitive (P2), and aversive outputs are intelligible defensive signals (DA1), and the architecture calibrates to developmental input (DA7), then the default reading of any mechanism output must be accurate to the environment the mechanism was calibrated for. Decoupling is the exception requiring evidence.

foundations.name: Inclusive Fitness
foundations.statement: Inclusive fitness is the loss function of selection, not of the organism's runtime computation. Inclusive fitness is one measure, Hamilton's: an individual's own reproductive success plus the reproductive success of relatives, weighted by how closely they are related. Survival counts because the dead do not reproduce.

foundations.name: Domain-Sensitive Interacting Adaptations
foundations.statement: The organism contains evolved, domain-sensitive, interacting functional adaptations.
foundations.derivation: Tooby & Cosmides (design principle), confirmed empirically by Panksepp, Bowlby, Dunbar, Boehm, Trivers, Gilbert, Rozin.

foundations.name: Systematic Mismatch
foundations.statement: Where modern environments depart from the conditions these adaptations evolved in, they push the adaptations outside their expected or regulatable operating ranges (graded forced). The departure runs in three modes: expected inputs missing, incompatible demands at once, and false cues that overstimulate the adaptations (graded strongly supported).
foundations.derivation: Eaton & Konner (discordance), Gluckman & Hanson (developmental mismatch), Li/van Vugt/Colarelli (mismatch review). Constrained by Boyd & Richerson / Henrich.

foundations.name: Defensive Signals Under Mismatch
foundations.statement: Where no clear physical defect is the cause, aversive outputs are intelligible defensive signals under mismatch, not evidence of defective design.
foundations.derivation: P2 + P3 + Nesse (negative outputs as defenses) + McEwen (reversible with environmental correction) + Birkett & Newton-Fisher (all 40 captive chimps studied showed abnormal behavior; none reported in wild observation).

foundations.name: Socially Scaffolded Regulation
foundations.statement: Human regulation is constitutively socially scaffolded (graded forced). Social context is the highest-leverage cross-cutting input dimension (graded strongly supported).
foundations.derivation: Dunbar + Coan & Sbarra (social baseline) + Bowlby (attachment) + Hrdy (cooperative breeding).

foundations.name: Recurrent Coupling and Cascading
foundations.statement: Systems are recurrently coupled; perturbations propagate and can self-maintain across domains.
foundations.derivation: Panksepp (cross-system inhibition) + Felitti (ACE dose-response) + Borsboom (network psychopathology) + McEwen (cumulative cross-system activation).

foundations.name: Proxy Hijacking via Open Loops
foundations.statement: Proxy cues can activate systems without meeting the conditions that normally regulate or terminate them.

foundations.name: Defensive Over-Activation Bias
foundations.statement: Defensive systems err toward over-activation under asymmetric error costs.
foundations.derivation: Haselton & Buss (error management) + Nesse (smoke detector) + P1.

foundations.name: Competing Motivational Programs
foundations.statement: The architecture contains partially competing motivational programs and tradeoff structures.
foundations.derivation: Trivers (parent-offspring conflict, reciprocal altruism) + Boehm (dominance + anti-dominance) + Gilbert (approach + submit).

foundations.name: Developmental Calibration
foundations.statement: The architecture calibrates to developmental and ongoing environmental input within evolved ranges.
foundations.derivation: Bowlby (internal working models) + Hrdy + McEwen + Meaney (HPA-axis calibration).

foundations.name: Phylogenetic Priority
foundations.statement: Priority runs by brain part. The old parts deep in the brain, similar in all mammals, produce emotion and fear without the newer outer layer: damage to the higher areas leaves the emotional responses of the lower areas in place, while damage to the lower areas compromises the emotional actions generated from the higher ones. The prefrontal cortex can hold the deep parts down, and stress that cannot be controlled, or that lasts, weakens it and switches control of behaviour and emotion to the older circuits.
foundations.derivation: Panksepp (affective circuits in ancient subcortical regions; stimulation and lesion studies across mammals) + Öhman and Mineka (fear responses without higher cortical processing) + Amat, Maier and colleagues (the prefrontal cortex holds the brainstem down when a stressor is controllable) + Arnsten, Sapolsky, Dias-Ferreira (stress weakens the prefrontal cortex).

foundations.name: Non-Substitutability of Mechanism Resolution
foundations.statement: Mechanism resolution conditions are not fully interchangeable. Improvement in one mechanism can buffer or modulate consequences in another, especially where mechanisms are recurrently coupled (DA3), but cross-system buffering does not generally replace the specific resolution conditions of an impaired mechanism. Well-being is often bottlenecked by severe unresolved deficits in individual mechanisms and is not well described as a simple average across mechanism states.
foundations.derivation: Follows from P2 (domain-sensitive interacting adaptations: if mechanisms are domain-sensitive, their resolution conditions are not freely interchangeable). Coupling and cross-system buffering effects are handled separately by DA3 (Recurrent Coupling and Cascading); DA9 specifically claims non-fungibility of resolution conditions, not absence of cross-system effects. Liebig's 1840 Law of the Minimum is the historical analogy for the bottleneck pattern.

foundations.name: Heritable Parameter Variation
foundations.statement: Architecture parameters (drive gains, thresholds, calibration setpoints) vary between individuals within heritable ranges.
foundations.derivation: Complements DA7: DA7 says the environment tunes the operating point, developmentally and ongoing; DA10 says the tunable ranges themselves differ per person, substantially heritably. Grounded by C15 triangulation across three independent method families: twin designs (Polderman et al. 2015 meta-analysis of fifty years of twin studies), adoption/family designs (Plomin program), and molecular SNP-heritability from unrelated individuals (Yang et al. 2010 GCTA line). Canonical framing: Turkheimer 2000 three laws of behavior genetics.

foundations.name: Allostatic Load Accumulation
foundations.statement: Chronic unresolved activation accumulates as allostatic load.

foundations.name: Market Proxy Exploitation
foundations.statement: Markets can industrialize proxy exploitation of unmet regulatory needs.
foundations.derivation: P3 + DA4 + market incentive structures + empirical (Moss food, Schull gambling, Haugen attention, Muldoon & Parke companion AI; children ate more after a single exposure to food adverts in the experiments pooled by Boyland et al. 2016).

foundations.name: Environment as Primary Intervention Layer
foundations.statement: Cortical override of subcortical activation is costly and tiring, and chronic defensive activation downregulates the cortical override machinery itself. Interventions that undo a mismatch, moving the organism's actual input conditions toward what it evolved for (the baseline rows of this atlas), are therefore more durable and less effort-dependent than interventions targeting cognitive override alone. The environment is a primary intervention layer for systemic and population-scale change, and is currently underweighted by major institutions.
foundations.derivation: Empirical corollary of DA8 (phylogenetic priority) + DA9 (non-fungibility of resolution conditions). DA8 + DA9 do not logically entail DC3 - they make environmental intervention a plausible higher-leverage path for systemic design, but the strength of the leverage is an empirical question. Supported by Sapolsky Forest Troop (N=1 troop, striking but limited generalization); Roseto Effect (observational, contested); Ilardi Therapeutic Lifestyle Change (author-reported response rates from a 2007 conference presentation and a 2009 trade book; no peer-reviewed RCT); BEIP foster care (single trial, large effect on reactive attachment disorder signs); captive-chimpanzee enrichment (variable but reproducible).

convergences.name: Threat-Detection via Ancient Subcortical Circuits
convergences.statement: Threat detection and defensive response are mediated by phylogenetically ancient subcortical circuits (amygdala, periaqueductal gray, hypothalamus) that operate pre-attentively and can override cortical processing - established independently by Panksepp's FEAR-system neuroanatomy, the Öhman/Mineka backward-masking fear-module research program, and Nesse's clinical evolutionary psychiatry linking panic and anxiety to these defensive systems.
independent_literatures: Öhman & Mineka fear module visual attention / backward masking
Nesse evolutionary psychiatry of panic and anxiety

convergences.name: Wanting-Liking Dissociation as Proxy Hijack
convergences.statement: Motivational pursuit ('wanting', mediated by mesolimbic dopamine) is dissociable from hedonic satisfaction ('liking'), creating an open-loop vulnerability where proxy cues can activate the SEEKING system without providing the conditions that normally terminate or resolve it - established independently by Berridge & Robinson's incentive-salience neuroscience, Tinbergen's supernormal-stimuli ethology, and Panksepp's SEEKING-circuit affective neuroscience.
independent_literatures: Berridge & Robinson incentive salience / mesolimbic dopamine

convergences.name: Socially Scaffolded Regulation via Attachment
convergences.statement: Human regulation is constitutively socially scaffolded: the organism's default expectation is proximity to trusted co-regulators, and this scaffolding is architectural rather than optional - established independently by Coan's Social Baseline Theory fMRI program, Bowlby's attachment theory, Hrdy's cooperative-breeding thesis, Dunbar's social-brain hypothesis, and Holt-Lunstad's mortality meta-analysis showing 50% survival advantage from strong social relationships.
independent_literatures: Coan social baseline theory affective neuroscience

convergences.name: Reciprocity, Norm Enforcement, and Coalition Architecture
convergences.statement: Humans have specialized architecture for reciprocal exchange, cheater detection, norm enforcement, and coalitional identity - supported independently by Fehr & Gächter's experimental altruistic-punishment findings, Boehm's reverse-dominance coalition dynamics in hunter-gatherer anthropology, and Tomasello's shared-intentionality comparative-cognition research.
independent_literatures: Fehr & Gächter experimental economics of cooperation
Tomasello comparative cognition and shared intentionality

convergences.name: Reproductive Motivation as Distinct Architecture
convergences.statement: Within reproductive motivation (desire, attraction, pair-bonding), sexual excitement runs on a distinct affective system, LUST, one of at least seven basic affective systems that Panksepp's cross-species brain stimulation, lesion and drug studies find in the ancient subcortical regions of mammalian brains. Men and women differ in what they prefer in a mate: across 37 cultures (Buss 1989), and again in 14,399 people in 45 countries (2016 sample), men on average preferred young and attractive partners more than women did, and women preferred partners with good financial prospects more than men did. As Haselton and Buss's error-management theory predicted, in their studies women underestimated men's commitment and men overestimated women's sexual intent. As Demismatch's own position, deduced from mismatch: everything that engages reproductive motivation sits on one ranking, from a real partner down to a pure stand-in such as pornography or an AI partner, ordered by how much of what reproductive motivation needs it supplies.
independent_literatures: Buss sex differences in mate preferences across cultures
Haselton & Buss error management in cross-sex mind reading

convergences.name: Domain-Sensitive Organism Architecture
convergences.statement: The human organism contains evolved, domain-sensitive, interacting functional adaptations rather than a general-purpose learner - supported independently by Tooby & Cosmides' design-principle derivation, Panksepp's conserved subcortical affective-motivational systems, and Bowlby's attachment-as-primary-motivational-system framework.
independent_literatures: Tooby & Cosmides evolutionary psychology design principle

convergences.name: Systematic EEA-Modern Environment Mismatch
convergences.statement: Modern post-agricultural, post-industrial environments push evolved adaptations outside their expected operating ranges in systematic and predictable ways - established independently by Eaton & Konner's discordance hypothesis, Li/van Vugt/Colarelli's mismatch-identification framework, Boyd & Richerson's gene-culture coevolution constraint (matched must include cultural scaffolding), and Henrich's WEIRD empirical diagnostic showing Western populations anchor the extreme end of the cross-cultural distribution.
independent_literatures: Eaton & Konner evolutionary medicine / discordance hypothesis
Li van Vugt Colarelli mismatch hypothesis review

convergences.name: Phylogenetic Conservation of Subcortical Affective Systems
convergences.statement: The core affective-motivational systems (SEEKING, FEAR, RAGE, CARE, PANIC/GRIEF, PLAY, LUST) are anatomically and functionally conserved across mammals and extend into birds for specific systems - established independently by Panksepp's deep-brain-stimulation and cross-species neuroscience, Bowlby's attachment cross-mammalian homology, and Hrdy's cross-primate parental/alloparental evidence.

convergences.name: Error Management Asymmetry in Defensive Systems
convergences.statement: Defensive systems evolved under asymmetric error costs err reliably toward over-activation (false-positive) because the cost of missing a true threat historically exceeded the cost of reacting to a non-threat - established independently by Nesse's smoke-detector principle in evolutionary psychiatry, Haselton & Buss's Error Management Theory in evolutionary social psychology, and the Öhman/Mineka fear-module visual-attention program in cognitive neuroscience.
independent_literatures: Nesse smoke detector principle evolutionary psychiatry
Öhman & Mineka fear module cognitive neuroscience

convergences.name: Allostatic Load Accumulation
convergences.statement: Chronic unresolved activation of stress-response systems produces cumulative physiological damage across multiple organ systems (allostatic load), reversible in part by environmental correction - established independently by McEwen's neuroendocrinology of allostasis and allostatic load and Sapolsky's primate stress physiology linking hierarchy type to cortisol and downstream pathology. The ACE Study was a third leg until 21 Nov 2026 and is withdrawn: it is a link from adults' own recall. The convergence now stands on two lines.
independent_literatures: McEwen allostasis and allostatic load neuroendocrinology

convergences.name: Inclusive Fitness as Loss Function
convergences.statement: Natural selection operates on inclusive fitness, one measure: an individual's own reproductive success plus the reproductive success of relatives, weighted by how closely they are related. Survival counts because the dead do not reproduce. This establishes a single loss function that all evolved motivational architecture serves, as demonstrated independently by Darwinian selection theory and Hamilton's kin-selection formalism.

convergences.name: Adverse Experience Cascading Dose-Response
convergences.statement: Chronic adverse load cascades across physiological systems, with effects that propagate and self-maintain across domains (metabolic, immune, neural, behavioral) - established independently by McEwen's allostatic-load neuroendocrinology and Panksepp's cross-system inhibition evidence for affective-system propagation. The ACE Study was a third leg, and the source of the word 'Dose-Response' in this convergence's name, until 21 Nov 2026 and is withdrawn: it is a link from adults' own recall (ext 1640), and about half of it is carried by genes and family for psychiatric outcomes (ext 1638). The convergence now stands on two lines.

convergences.name: Heritable Individual Variation in Behavioral Traits
convergences.statement: Individual differences in human behavioral and psychological traits are substantially heritable in every adequately measured domain, established independently by twin designs (Polderman et al. 2015 meta-analysis of fifty years of twin studies: 17,804 traits from 2,748 publications, average reported heritability 49%), adoption and family designs (the Plomin program: significant genetic influence on all psychological traits with corroborating adoption evidence), and molecular SNP-heritability estimated from unrelated individuals (the Yang et al. 2010 GCTA line), with Turkheimer's three laws of behavior genetics as the canonical framing. Heritability is a population statistic under a given environment distribution, not individual determinism.
independent_literatures: Plomin adoption and family designs (behavior genetics)

convergences.name: Aversive Outputs as Intelligible Defensive Signals
convergences.statement: Where no clear physical defect is the cause, aversive psychological and physiological outputs (anxiety, low mood, pain, grief, fatigue, anger) are intelligible defensive signals produced by architecture that is functioning correctly in response to inputs outside its expected operating range - established independently by Nesse's 'good reasons for bad feelings' evolutionary psychiatry, Panksepp's affective neuroscience of conserved aversive systems, and Fehr & Gächter's finding that anger/moralistic outrage is the proximate mechanism for prosocial norm enforcement rather than a dysregulation.
independent_literatures: Nesse evolutionary psychiatry of defensive signals
Panksepp affective neuroscience of aversive systems
Fehr & Gächter experimental economics of moralistic outrage

convergences.name: Developmental Calibration within Evolved Ranges
convergences.statement: Specific physiological and behavioral systems calibrate during specific developmental windows to environmental inputs within evolved parameters; inputs far outside those parameters leave a lasting mark - established independently by the Bucharest randomised trial of foster care against institutional rearing, the English and Romanian Adoptees natural experiment, and cross-fostering experiments in rats, with McEwen's HPA-axis neuroendocrinology as the bodily route. Inside the ordinary range of homes, differences in upbringing explain little of how adults differ in personality: adoptive siblings reared together correlate .04 (ext 2880). Attachment in infancy showed no significant link with attachment more than 15 years later (ext 2893). Recalled childhood adversity (the ACE Study) was a leg of this convergence until 21 Nov 2026 and is withdrawn: it is a link from adults' own recall.
independent_literatures: Nelson, Zeanah and Fox Bucharest Early Intervention Project (randomised trial)
Rutter and Sonuga-Barke English and Romanian Adoptees study (natural experiment)
Meaney and Francis cross-fostering in rats (experimental neuroendocrinology)

mechanisms.name: Threat Management
mechanisms.description: Defensive system responding to threat cues. Includes offensive mode (frustration-aggression) absorbed from old M3 RAGE.
mechanisms.eli5: Detects danger. Makes you freeze, fight, or flee.
mechanisms.resolution_conditions: Safety established, threat eliminated or avoided.
mechanisms.mismatch_prediction: Modern threats - debt, emails, social media, status anxiety - can't be fought or fled. System stays on.
mechanisms.phylogenetic_age: ~460-535Myr (defence centre, all vertebrates); amygdala circuit ~340Myr+ (four-limbed vertebrates)

proxy_gradient.raw: 5 levels (resolvability/actionability axis; true DA4 proxy only at floor): acute danger you can fight/flee then escape (FULL) → real present threat resolved by a trusted other (PARTIAL) → chronic slow-burn real threat, no terminating action (MIXED) → abstract/anticipated threat, no physical target (MINIMAL) → engineered supernormal outrage/threat media (ZERO; CONTESTABLE)
proxy_gradient.preamble: 5 levels (resolvability/actionability axis; true DA4 proxy only at floor)

levels.label: acute danger you can fight/flee then escape
real present threat resolved by a trusted other
chronic slow-burn real threat, no terminating action
abstract/anticipated threat, no physical target
engineered supernormal outrage/threat media

sex_diff.raw: ext 733: A meta-analysis found that males are more physically aggressive than females at all ages and across cultures, while girls show more indirect aggression than boys only in later childhood and adolescence, depending on how it is measured. ext 2711: In the first of four experiments, both men and women underestimated the time to arrival of approaching sounds, more strongly among women; in the others women also judged approaching sounds that stopped short of them as closer than men did, while no sex difference appeared for sounds moving away. ext 2581 (before a public speech): Men supported by their partner showed a significantly smaller cortisol response than unsupported or stranger-supported men. Women showed no drop with stranger support and a tendency toward a larger cortisol response when supported by their boyfriend. ext 3667 (driving simulator): men drove more aggressively than women (d = 0.06).

forced_by_convergence.name: Threat-Detection via Ancient Subcortical Circuits
forced_by_convergence.statement: Threat detection and defensive response are mediated by phylogenetically ancient subcortical circuits (amygdala, periaqueductal gray, hypothalamus) that operate pre-attentively and can override cortical processing - established independently by Panksepp's FEAR-system neuroanatomy, the Öhman/Mineka backward-masking fear-module research program, and Nesse's clinical evolutionary psychiatry linking panic and anxiety to these defensive systems.

mechanisms.name: Pursuit / Exploration
mechanisms.description: General-purpose seeking system. The same wanting system also runs when what is wanted is a partner: in human brain imaging the networks for sex are comparable to those for other rewards and follow the same phases of wanting, liking and satiety (ext 2724), and in male rats accumbens dopamine rose again during mating with a new receptive female (ext 2285). What is specific to partners belongs to M14. M2 resolves through real-world challenges that produce tangible outcomes: goal progress, skill building, resource acquisition. Cor reads the low-drive, low-pleasure state that Western scales score as anhedonic depression as SEEKING underactivation (Panksepp 1998, ext 264). Where a clear physical defect is behind the dopamine decline, that case sits on the physical side of the clear-defect rule; otherwise it is a response state.
mechanisms.eli5: Drives you to explore, pursue goals, and engage with the world.
mechanisms.resolution_conditions: Engagement with real challenges producing tangible outcomes.
mechanisms.mismatch_prediction: Variable-reward apps fire SEEKING without resolution. Open loop. Cor's reading of the net effect of slot machine design (ext 72): SEEKING/wanting circuits fire continuously on random-ratio reinforcement while actual satisfaction (liking) never arrives.
mechanisms.phylogenetic_age: ~460-535Myr (dopamine basal ganglia, all vertebrates; contested); reward pathway ~165Myr+ (mammals)

proxy_gradient.raw: 5 levels (cue constant = SEEKING/wanting; ordered by tangible outcome + consummatory-liking closure supplied, not by cue strength): engaging a real challenge that yields a real outcome (FULL) → knowledge work with a real but abstracted, delayed outcome (PARTIAL) → variable-reward app/feed with intermittent real payoff (MIXED) → infinite novelty, content scroll/idle browsing (MINIMAL) → machine gambling engineered for time-on-device with guaranteed net loss (ZERO). The order of MIXED (app) and MINIMAL (scroll) is untested.
proxy_gradient.preamble: 5 levels (cue constant = SEEKING/wanting; ordered by tangible outcome + consummatory-liking closure supplied, not by cue strength)
proxy_gradient.trailing: The order of MIXED (app) and MINIMAL (scroll) is untested.

knowledge work with a real but abstracted, delayed outcome
variable-reward app/feed with intermittent real payoff
infinite novelty, content scroll/idle browsing
machine gambling engineered for time-on-device with guaranteed net loss

forced_by_convergence.statement: Motivational pursuit ('wanting', mediated by mesolimbic dopamine) is dissociable from hedonic satisfaction ('liking'), creating an open-loop vulnerability where proxy cues can activate the SEEKING system without providing the conditions that normally terminate or resolve it - established independently by Berridge & Robinson's incentive-salience neuroscience, Tinbergen's supernormal-stimuli ethology, and Panksepp's SEEKING-circuit affective neuroscience.

mechanisms.name: Social Bonding
mechanisms.description: Attachment and co-regulation system. Includes grief mode (absorbed from old M9 GRIEF). Two states: security (enables broadly) and grief (suppresses broadly). Cor reads grief and the low mood that follows loss (what Western scales score as depression) as states of an opioid-modulated affective circuit rather than purely cognitive states (Panksepp, ext 259).
mechanisms.eli5: Forms bonds with other humans. Pain-grade distress when they're gone.
mechanisms.resolution_conditions: Reliable human co-regulation through physical presence, operating through nested social layers: ~5 intimate co-regulators (primary emotional/physical support), ~15 sympathy group, ~50 close social partners, ~150 coherent face-to-face relationships (Dunbar number - outer cognitive ceiling). Each layer represents qualitatively different relationship types with different obligations and investment requirements. The innermost ~5 provide the majority of social regulation; the critical variable at this layer is reliability, not count. The ~150 outer figure is an illustrative central tendency, not a hard limit: its derivation from the primate neocortex-ratio regression is contested (Lindenfors, Wartel & Lind 2021). What the evidence carries is the nested layering and the reliability-over-count point, not the exact rung figures; the layered structure and its low-hundreds clustering are separately observed in phone, Christmas-card, and Facebook data.
mechanisms.mismatch_prediction: Nuclear family, isolated living, mediated contact substituting for physical presence. Cor's reading of Dunbar's proposal that face-to-face meetings are needed to keep friendships from sliding down the network layers (ext 509): this fits the claim that the bonding system needs physical co-presence.
mechanisms.phylogenetic_age: ~165-200Myr (attachment, mammals); human layered network not dated

proxy_gradient.raw: 5 levels (ordered by real co-regulatory function supplied, not amount of contact): reliable physically co-present inner circle (FULL) → real bonded inner circle held at a distance, remote contact (PARTIAL) → large mediated network routing only partly to real co-presence (MIXED) → one-sided parasocial attachment to a non-reciprocating figure (MINIMAL) → AI companion engineered to simulate a reciprocating bond (ZERO; theoretical on ext595). Off-gradient: isolated/solo living = empty-shelf deprivation, not a rung.
proxy_gradient.preamble: 5 levels (ordered by real co-regulatory function supplied, not amount of contact)
proxy_gradient.trailing: Off-gradient: isolated/solo living = empty-shelf deprivation, not a rung.

levels.label: reliable physically co-present inner circle
real bonded inner circle held at a distance, remote contact
large mediated network routing only partly to real co-presence
one-sided parasocial attachment to a non-reciprocating figure
AI companion engineered to simulate a reciprocating bond

sex_diff.raw: E4722: the wish to affiliate with others under stress is much stronger in women than in men; "seeking and using social support" showed the largest difference, and of 26 studies that tested for it, 25 favoured women, one found no difference and none went the other way. E5450: overall, men scored higher on avoidance and lower on attachment anxiety than women, with substantial heterogeneity between studies. E2581: men supported by their partner showed a significantly smaller cortisol response than unsupported or stranger-supported men; women showed no drop with stranger support and a tendency toward a larger cortisol response when supported by their boyfriend. E755: women cried more often than men during bereavement. E3726 (rhesus macaques): the effects of removing the mother for a few days varied with the length of the separation and the infant's sex. E5519 (rhesus macaques): male infants played more during this time and female infants played less and groomed others more.

mechanisms.name: Social Calibration / Play
mechanisms.description: Play system develops social skills. Play often disappears when animals are under fitness challenge and remains absent under chronic or severe stress. It can also increase in stressful situations, in response to reduced parental care, or as a rebound after a period of deprivation.
mechanisms.eli5: Learns social rules through rough-and-tumble play. Requires real playmates.
mechanisms.resolution_conditions: Self-directed, unsupervised physical play with other children. In forager childhoods this is a mixed-age group.
mechanisms.mismatch_prediction: Structured activities replacing free play. Screens replacing bodies. Play deprivation.
mechanisms.phylogenetic_age: ~60Myr+ (social play, all primates; up to ~170Myr if one mammal system); play in reptiles and fish arose separately

proxy_gradient.raw: 5 levels (cue ≈ constant PLAY/SEEKING social-joy pull, fired in attenuated/substitute form at lower screen levels; ordered by how much real embodied reciprocity with an identity-bearing partner survives): self-directed, unsupervised physical play with other children, mixed-age as in forager childhoods (FULL) → adult-structured supervised physical activity, organized sports (PARTIAL) → screen-mediated multiplayer play with real peers (MIXED) → solitary single-player screen play, no reciprocating partner (MINIMAL) → engineered companion-AI / supernormal variable-reward 'play' product (ZERO; architecture-derived). The order of MIXED (screen play with real peers) and MINIMAL (solitary game) is untested.
proxy_gradient.preamble: 5 levels (cue ≈ constant PLAY/SEEKING social-joy pull, fired in attenuated/substitute form at lower screen levels; ordered by how much real embodied reciprocity with an identity-bearing partner survives)
proxy_gradient.trailing: The order of MIXED (screen play with real peers) and MINIMAL (solitary game) is untested.

adult-structured supervised physical activity, organized sports
screen-mediated multiplayer play with real peers
solitary single-player screen play, no reciprocating partner

E2249 (Hadza and BaYaka children and adolescents aged 3 to 18): adolescent girls played less than younger girls while adolescent boys did not. E3535 (23 nine-year-old children): longer confinement went with more exercise play for boys and more social sedentary behaviour for girls at playtime. E3750 (free-living juvenile Belding's ground squirrels): perinatal testosterone raised the sexual play started by young females to near male rates and did not change play fighting.

mechanisms.name: Status Monitoring
mechanisms.description: Rank regulation. Shame, pride, submission, defeat, rank vigilance. Not optional - runs continuously.
mechanisms.eli5: Constantly monitors where you stand relative to others.
mechanisms.resolution_conditions: Acceptable position in a bounded, personally-known reference group on the order of ~150 (an illustrative central tendency, not a hard number; the precise figure is contested per Lindenfors 2021). Earned prestige preferred over coerced dominance. Prestige and dominance are separate routes to rank (Henrich & Gil-White 2001, work 129; Cheng et al. 2013, ext 622). Among the Chabu, prestige predicted elected leadership more strongly than dominance (Garfield & Hagen 2020, ext 624). Among Tsimane men, both routes went with higher fertility, and prestige was the strongest path from status to fitness (von Rueden et al. 2011, ext 623).
mechanisms.mismatch_prediction: Global comparison via social media. Millions of "peers." Status-defeat cascade. Cor's reading of Gilbert's account of shame as an evolved submissive defense (ext 482): it turns costly when modern status comparison (social media, workplace evaluation, academic competition) keeps it activated.
mechanisms.phylogenetic_age: ~420-445Myr (rank circuit, bony vertebrates); rank-linked health ~25-34Myr+ (Old World primates)

mechanisms.name: Circadian Regulation
mechanisms.description: SCN master clock. Gates metabolism, immunity, cognition, mood. The mismatch lies in timing more than in sleep duration. A week of natural light moved the body clock about two hours earlier while sleep duration stayed the same (Wright et al. 2013, ext 610, n=8). Social jetlag predicts overweight after controlling for sleep duration (Roenneberg et al. 2012, ext 92). Across 43 studies of 231,648 people, social jetlag went with higher body mass index and 1.2 times the odds of overweight (Arab et al. 2024). Cor's reading of the finding that judges rate sleep-deprived people as less healthy and less attractive from photographs alone (ext 438): this makes sleep a phenotypic fitness signal: the physiological state produced by adequate sleep is visible to potential mates and social partners, and sleep loss degrades that signal.
mechanisms.eli5: Synchronizes every system to the light-dark cycle. Master timing architecture.
mechanisms.resolution_conditions: Dark-cued sleep onset, bright daylight exposure, consistent rhythm.
mechanisms.mismatch_prediction: Electric light, blue screens, shift work, caffeine
mechanisms.phylogenetic_age: ~500Myr+ (animal clock genes, insects and vertebrates); cyanobacterial clocks are older but a separate origin

mechanisms.name: Care / Alloparenting
mechanisms.description: Parental and alloparental care system. Oxytocin/prolactin circuits. Cor reads maternal ambivalence as adaptive rather than pathological (Hrdy, ext 281).
mechanisms.eli5: Distributed care - the organism expects a village, not solo parenting.
mechanisms.resolution_conditions: A distributed care network rather than solo or dyadic parenting. In forager societies people other than the mother hold and care for infants: Hadza allomothers do about 31% of the holding of infants under four (Crittenden and Marlowe 2008, ext 2128), and Efe infants are cared for by many people from birth (Tronick et al. 1987, ext 700). The critical resolving variable is the presence + continuity of real alloparental supply (care + provisioning), NOT bare kinship.
mechanisms.mismatch_prediction: Nuclear family without alloparental network. Parent burnout cascade.

proxy_gradient.raw: Two scales. Axis A - real alloparental supply (empty-shelf/deprivation axis; ordered by caregiver count × continuity, NOT kinship): distributed kin-and-community network (FULL) → multiple reliable caregivers incl. high-quality paid care (REDUCED) → single intermittent helper / high-turnover institutional care (THIN) → solo/dyadic parent, no network (EMPTY SHELF; deprivation floor, not a proxy). Axis B - fake-fix proxy (real alloparental function ≈0 for both; ordered by completeness of the caregiver-OTHER counterfeit): screen/app babysitter → AI/robot 'caregiver' (ZERO; architecture-derived).

forced_by_convergence.name: Inclusive Fitness as Loss Function
forced_by_convergence.statement: Natural selection operates on inclusive fitness, one measure: an individual's own reproductive success plus the reproductive success of relatives, weighted by how closely they are related. Survival counts because the dead do not reproduce. This establishes a single loss function that all evolved motivational architecture serves, as demonstrated independently by Darwinian selection theory and Hamilton's kin-selection formalism.

mechanisms.name: Movement
mechanisms.description: Physical activity as zeitgeber, anti-inflammatory, mood regulator.
mechanisms.eli5: Movement isn't just exercise - it activates repair mechanisms throughout the organism.
mechanisms.resolution_conditions: Movement that's part of daily life rather than set aside as 'exercise'. Hadza men walk about 11 to 13 km a day and women about 6 to 8 km (Pontzer et al. 2012 and Wood et al. 2021, GPS; ext 2430, ext 3418), and the women also dig for several hours (Lieberman 2021, ext 196), all as a side effect of foraging (Hadza only).
mechanisms.mismatch_prediction: Sedentarism. Gym sessions as partial compensation.
mechanisms.phylogenetic_age: ~2Myr (human form, argued); older regulatory roles not dated

mechanisms.name: Cooperation / Alliance
mechanisms.description: Reciprocity + norm enforcement + alliance dynamics. Convergence C11 forces M11. Three bodies of tests support it (Fehr & Gächter, Boehm, Tomasello), with Trivers 1971 as the theory behind them.
mechanisms.eli5: Reciprocal exchange, cheater detection, coalitional identity.
mechanisms.resolution_conditions: Trusted reciprocal network with norm enforcement within a group small enough for direct reputation tracking (on the order of ~150 - the same low-hundreds ceiling that bounds M3; the precise figure is contested per Lindenfors 2021). Norm enforcement requires repeated direct interaction where defectors can be identified, remembered, and sanctioned. Beyond that ceiling, cooperation requires institutional scaffolding (formal rules, third-party enforcement, shared fictions) rather than direct reciprocity. No shared fiction at the direct-reciprocity layer.
mechanisms.mismatch_prediction: Anonymous transactions, ghosting, no shared narrative.
mechanisms.phylogenetic_age: ~25-34Myr+ (reciprocity, Old World primates); human norm enforcement under ~10Myr

mechanisms.name: Contamination Avoidance
mechanisms.description: Three kinds of disgust, pathogen, sexual and moral: ratings of how disgusting acts and objects are fall into these three factors (ext 3414). How the moral kind began is left open. Behavioral immune system.
mechanisms.eli5: Disgust system. It pulls you back from germs, from some sexual acts and partners, and from moral violations.
mechanisms.resolution_conditions: Clean food, clean social environment, moral disgust contained.
mechanisms.mismatch_prediction: Moral disgust weaponized in politics, purity spirals.

forced_by_convergence.name: Domain-Sensitive Organism Architecture
forced_by_convergence.statement: The human organism contains evolved, domain-sensitive, interacting functional adaptations rather than a general-purpose learner - supported independently by Tooby & Cosmides' design-principle derivation, Panksepp's conserved subcortical affective-motivational systems, and Bowlby's attachment-as-primary-motivational-system framework.

forced_by_convergence.name: Error Management Asymmetry in Defensive Systems
forced_by_convergence.statement: Defensive systems evolved under asymmetric error costs err reliably toward over-activation (false-positive) because the cost of missing a true threat historically exceeded the cost of reacting to a non-threat - established independently by Nesse's smoke-detector principle in evolutionary psychiatry, Haselton & Buss's Error Management Theory in evolutionary social psychology, and the Öhman/Mineka fear-module visual-attention program in cognitive neuroscience.

mechanisms.name: Energy Regulation
mechanisms.description: Pontzer's constrained energy model. Part of the energy spent in activity is offset by lower basal expenditure: about 28 percent in adults living ordinary lives (ext 2346).
mechanisms.eli5: Hunger, satiety, and constrained total energy expenditure.
mechanisms.resolution_conditions: Effortful, diverse, seasonal whole foods. Metabolic variety.
mechanisms.mismatch_prediction: Ultra-processed foods defeating satiety signals. Cor reads chronic arterial inflammation as a paradigm case of allostatic load from metabolic mismatch (ext 426).
mechanisms.phylogenetic_age: ~420Myr+ (appetite brake, jawed vertebrates); human energy budget under ~10Myr

forced_by_convergence.name: Systematic EEA-Modern Environment Mismatch
forced_by_convergence.statement: Modern post-agricultural, post-industrial environments push evolved adaptations outside their expected operating ranges in systematic and predictable ways - established independently by Eaton & Konner's discordance hypothesis, Li/van Vugt/Colarelli's mismatch-identification framework, Boyd & Richerson's gene-culture coevolution constraint (matched must include cultural scaffolding), and Henrich's WEIRD empirical diagnostic showing Western populations anchor the extreme end of the cross-cultural distribution.

forced_by_convergence.name: Wanting-Liking Dissociation as Proxy Hijack
forced_by_convergence.statement: Motivational pursuit ('wanting', mediated by mesolimbic dopamine) is dissociable from hedonic satisfaction ('liking'), creating an open-loop vulnerability where proxy cues can activate the SEEKING system without providing the conditions that normally terminate or resolve it - established independently by Berridge & Robinson's incentive-salience neuroscience, Tinbergen's supernormal-stimuli ethology, and Panksepp's SEEKING-circuit affective neuroscience.

forced_by_convergence.name: Allostatic Load Accumulation
forced_by_convergence.statement: Chronic unresolved activation of stress-response systems produces cumulative physiological damage across multiple organ systems (allostatic load), reversible in part by environmental correction - established independently by McEwen's neuroendocrinology of allostasis and allostatic load and Sapolsky's primate stress physiology linking hierarchy type to cortisol and downstream pathology. The ACE Study was a third leg until 21 Nov 2026 and is withdrawn: it is a link from adults' own recall. The convergence now stands on two lines.

mechanisms.name: Reproductive Motivation
mechanisms.description: Fisher's three-system model. HPG axis, not just brain circuits.
mechanisms.eli5: Three components - desire, attraction, and pair bonding - that can work independently of each other. This system shapes much more of human behavior than reproduction itself.
mechanisms.resolution_conditions: Sexual fulfillment within pair bond + a couple that lasts long enough to raise the children + reproductive success.
mechanisms.mismatch_prediction: Pornography, dating apps, delayed reproduction, social media mate-value comparison.
mechanisms.phylogenetic_age: ~460-535Myr (sexual hormone axis, all vertebrates); human pair bond ~2-4Myr (contested)

forced_by_convergence.name: Reproductive Motivation as Distinct Architecture
forced_by_convergence.statement: Within reproductive motivation (desire, attraction, pair-bonding), sexual excitement runs on a distinct affective system, LUST, one of at least seven basic affective systems that Panksepp's cross-species brain stimulation, lesion and drug studies find in the ancient subcortical regions of mammalian brains. Men and women differ in what they prefer in a mate: across 37 cultures (Buss 1989), and again in 14,399 people in 45 countries (2016 sample), men on average preferred young and attractive partners more than women did, and women preferred partners with good financial prospects more than men did. As Haselton and Buss's error-management theory predicted, in their studies women underestimated men's commitment and men overestimated women's sexual intent. As Demismatch's own position, deduced from mismatch: everything that engages reproductive motivation sits on one ranking, from a real partner down to a pure stand-in such as pornography or an AI partner, ordered by how much of what reproductive motivation needs it supplies.

mechanisms.name: Touch
mechanisms.description: Touch carried by C-tactile afferents, an input to M3. People want it: the more days people had spent in lockdown, the more touch they wanted, most of all intimate touch (ext 2775). It also acts under threat: married women holding their husband's hand under threat of shock showed a broad drop in activation of threat-response systems (ext 2270).
mechanisms.resolution_conditions: Regular physical contact with trusted others.
mechanisms.mismatch_prediction: Touch-starved modern environments. Kangaroo-care evidence: large developmental and autonomic gains from skin-to-skin care (ED9). In low-birthweight infants, mostly enrolled after stabilization, kangaroo mother care was associated with a reduction in the risk of mortality at discharge or 40 to 41 weeks' postmenstrual age (risk ratio 0.60; eight trials, 1736 infants; ext 618). Among low-birthweight newborns, kangaroo mother care compared to conventional care was associated with 36% lower mortality (RR 0.64; ext 3103).

forced_by_convergence.name: Phylogenetic Conservation of Subcortical Affective Systems
forced_by_convergence.statement: The core affective-motivational systems (SEEKING, FEAR, RAGE, CARE, PANIC/GRIEF, PLAY, LUST) are anatomically and functionally conserved across mammals and extend into birds for specific systems - established independently by Panksepp's deep-brain-stimulation and cross-species neuroscience, Bowlby's attachment cross-mammalian homology, and Hrdy's cross-primate parental/alloparental evidence.

forced_by_convergence.name: Socially Scaffolded Regulation via Attachment
forced_by_convergence.statement: Human regulation is constitutively socially scaffolded: the organism's default expectation is proximity to trusted co-regulators, and this scaffolding is architectural rather than optional - established independently by Coan's Social Baseline Theory fMRI program, Bowlby's attachment theory, Hrdy's cooperative-breeding thesis, Dunbar's social-brain hypothesis, and Holt-Lunstad's mortality meta-analysis showing 50% survival advantage from strong social relationships.

parameters.name: Social network layers (~5/15/50/150)
parameters.eea_baseline: The ancestral social world was structured as a series of hierarchically inclusive, nested relationship layers, each roughly three times the size of the one inside it: an innermost support clique of ~5 close confidants who provided emotional and physical support, a sympathy group of ~15 (contacted at least monthly), an affinity/band layer of ~50 (the typical overnight foraging camp), and an active personal network of ~150 (the outer ceiling of stable, individually-known relationships). Each layer carried a qualitatively different grade of intimacy and contact frequency, with the heaviest investment concentrated in the inner ~5-15. The ~150 outer figure is an illustrative central tendency, not a constant: traditional tribal and clan groupings cluster in the low hundreds. Its original derivation from the primate neocortex-ratio regression fails re-analysis (Lindenfors, Wartel and Lind 2021), so the specific number is treated as approximate; what is load-bearing is the nested layering, not the precise ceiling. This was the full architecture within which status was monitored and alliances tracked: a personally-known reference group bounded at ~150, not an anonymous mass. Human social groups cluster at characteristic values of approximately 5, 12, 35, 150, 500, and 2,000 (ext 490). Forager populations were organized in nested levels, with each level about three to four times larger than the one below it, from families through camps to regional groups (ext 685).

layer_sizes.affinity_band: 50, the typical hunter-gatherer overnight camp (ext 404); 35, the band (ext 490)

eea_value.scaling_factor: approximately three (ext 404); about three to four in forager population structure, a constant ratio close to 4 (ext 685)
eea_value.outer_ceiling_note: low hundreds; ~150 is an approximate central tendency, not a constant; the neocortex-ratio derivation is contested (Lindenfors 2021)

parameters.modern_default: The modern environment delivers a radically inverted network shape: nominal friend counts that for a small minority run to many hundreds or thousands (ext 4624), while the layers that actually carry support and intimacy stay capacity-bounded. Online networks reproduce the same ~5/15 inner structure when genuine ties are measured (support clique ~4, sympathy group ~14, not significantly different from offline values), and mean platform friend counts hover near ~150-190 (across all 721 million Facebook users of May 2011 the mean was about 190 and the median 99; Ugander et al. 2011, ext 4624), but the bulk of nominal connections are not considered close friends (only ~27.6% of Facebook friends are considered 'genuine' (i.e. close) friends, ext 508). Dunbar proposes that face-to-face meetings are needed from time to time to keep friendships from sliding down the network layers until they become mere acquaintances, and that social media may slow this decay and cannot replace in-person contact (ext 509). The result is a wide, shallow periphery of weak or fictive ties layered on top of a core that the larger network does not enlarge: among 117 adults, more time on social media went with more online friends and with no larger or emotionally closer offline network (Pollet, Roberts and Dunbar 2011).
parameters.gap_statement: The mismatch is between the number of ties the modern environment presents (a mean of about 190 Facebook friends, and many hundreds or thousands for a small minority, ext 4624) and the number the brain can actually monitor and invest in (~150, with real support concentrated in the inner ~5-15). People with large networks had on average weaker ties, measured as time spent calling (ext 4349). Status monitoring (M5) and alliance/reputation tracking (M11), evolved for a ~150 personally-known reference group, are now flooded by reference groups, while the trust-bearing inner layers remain capped and are under-fed when face-to-face contact is displaced.
parameters.confidence_note: Grade, rubric v2 (22 Nov 2026): tested many times for the layering. Forager populations were organised in nested levels, each about three to four times the size of the one below, across 339 societies in Binford's compilation (Hamilton et al. 2007, ext 1048: families of about 4.5, dispersed groups of 15.6, residential groups of 54, periodic gatherings of 165). Personal networks fall into nested layers about three times the size of the one inside in pooled published group sizes (Zhou et al. 2005, ext 2042), phone records of the 26,680 users who called at least 100 others (Mac Carron, Kaski and Dunbar 2016, ext 2026), and Facebook and Twitter contact data (Dunbar et al. 2015, ext 4336; Arnaboldi et al. 2016, ext 3323). A model with one fixed capacity for relationships, in which closer ties cost more, reproduces the layers, and about 98 percent of 84 students' networks showed them with a scaling ratio of about 2.7 to 3.1 (Tamarit et al. 2018). Main weakness: the forager levels are group sizes, not one person's network, and the modern network data all come from Dunbar's group and its collaborators. The 150 figure fails re-analysis of the primate regression it came from (Lindenfors, Wartel and Lind 2021, ext 619), so the layer sizes and the 150 ceiling are approximate. Forager residential groups are fluid (Bird et al. 2019, ext 684), which concerns who shares a camp, not the layers of a person's network.

parameters.name: Lifetime known-individual pool (~1,000)
parameters.eea_baseline: Across a foraging lifetime an individual accumulated a bounded pool of personally known others. Estimates put this cumulative lifetime roster at roughly 1,000+ distinct individuals (Hill et al. 2014, Hadza/Ache), much greater than the predicted 150 significant social interactants (Dunbar's number) that was extrapolated from primate brain by social group size regressions. This pool was not a single contemporaneous group: it accreted over decades through camp reshuffling, regional fission-fusion, and durable cross-camp partnerships (e.g. Ju/'hoansi hxaro). The cognitive machinery for naming, tracking reputation, and gauging trust was calibrated to a lifetime ceiling on this order, with the ~150 active-network limit (Dunbar) operating as the concurrent sub-ceiling within it.

parameters.name: Within-camp kin fraction (low; campmates mostly unrelated)
parameters.eea_baseline: A person's residential camp/band was NOT a clan of close relatives. Across forager societies the typical residential group (~28 adults) was composed mostly of individuals to whom the focal person was not closely related: primary/first-order kin (parents, siblings, offspring) made up only a small minority of co-residents (under 10% of a residential camp; Apicella et al. 2012, ext 601), and most campmates were unrelated or only distantly related. An agent-based model suggests that, even if all individuals seek to live with as many kin as possible, within-camp relatedness is reduced if men and women have equal influence in selecting camp members (Dyble et al. 2015, ext 687).

parameters.modern_default: Modern social environments invert the ancestral pattern in two opposite directions at once. (1) The family one is related to is, for about two in three US adults aged 25 or over with a living parent or adult child, not all within 30 miles (three in four have one within 30 miles, about a third have all of them that near, and 13 percent share a home with one; Choi et al. 2020, ext 4204). (2) The larger groups one spends daily life inside (workplace, neighborhood, online networks, institutions) are NOT self-assembled through mutual choice, reciprocity, and reputation tracking; membership is assigned by employment, address, or platform. The result is that 'who you live and work among' is no longer the output of a relationship-selection process; it is administratively or commercially determined.
parameters.gap_statement: The ancestral signal was: 'the group around me is mostly unrelated people I (or my band) actively chose and continuously vetted through reciprocity and reputation; kinship is not what holds us together, the relationships are.' The modern signal is degraded on the selection axis: the unrelated people around us are still mostly unrelated (that part matches), but they are assigned rather than chosen, and the reciprocity/reputation machinery that turned unrelated campmates into durable trusted allies is largely absent or shallow. Mechanisms M3 (bonding) and M11 (cooperation/alliance) evolved expecting that low kin-relatedness would be compensated by self-selected, reciprocal, reputation-anchored dyads. Modernity delivers the low relatedness WITHOUT the compensating chosen-and-vetted dyadic structure, so the mechanisms fire in a world of unrelated-but-also-unbonded co-residents, which is a key part of why being surrounded by people can still register as social isolation.

parameters.name: Membership turnover (camp dissolves and reconstitutes; most campmates change between survey waves)
parameters.eea_baseline: The residential group (camp/band) was a fission-fusion structure that continuously dissolved and reconstituted rather than a fixed-membership unit. Among the Hadza, entire camps relocated roughly every 4-8 weeks and individuals reshuffled across camps such that only a minority of campmates carried over from one survey wave to the next (Smith et al. 2018, Hadza waves 1 to 3 years apart; the exact proportion is unverified, see eea_value). Crucially, despite this high residential churn, assortment on cooperation persisted (cooperators clustered together across reshuffles). Group composition was fluid.

Waves are 1 to 3 years apart, so neither is an annual rate.

parameters.modern_default: Modern social environments invert the structure: the GROUP labels are stable and durable (a workplace, a school cohort, a neighborhood, a social-media platform or feed) while the actual dyadic relationships within them are shallow, interchangeable, and disposable. People remain nominal members of named, persistent groups, yet cycle through co-members with little individual reciprocal investment, and there is no institution analogous to a delayed-reciprocity partnership (e.g. hxaro) that conserves a specific bond once physical proximity ends. In a Dutch panel followed over seven years, a lack of opportunities to meet (in contexts such as work, family, sports clubs, voluntary associations and the neighbourhood) was an important reason why many relationships ended (Mollenhorst, Volker and Flap 2014, ext 2649).
parameters.gap_statement: The ancestral and modern environments are inverted on which layer is stable. Ancestrally the GROUP churned (most campmates changed between survey waves). Modernity delivers the opposite: stable, durable group labels (workplace, cohort, feed) paired with shallow, disposable dyads and no mechanism (no hxaro-equivalent) for conserving a specific bond once proximity ends. The mismatch lies in where turnover lands: on the relationships, which evolved to persist, instead of on group membership, which evolved to be fluid. That leaves the co-regulating, reputation-tracking reciprocal dyad chronically unmet.
parameters.resolution_unit: The durable reciprocal dyad - a specific, individually-known partner with whom reciprocity, co-regulation, and reputation are tracked over years. What needs conserving across membership turnover is not the group or the amount of contact but the persistence of particular bonded relationships; the bond, not the band, is the conserved unit.

parameters.name: Selection rule / "shuffle algorithm" (choice-driven; homophily + cooperation + reciprocity)
parameters.eea_baseline: Who you lived alongside was produced by an ongoing, choice-driven assortment process operating across frequent residential reshuffling. In Hadza camps this "algorithm" had recurring structure: (1) homophily - in both the campmate and gift networks, social ties were more likely between people similar in age, height, weight, body fat, and handgrip strength; (2) strong reciprocity - in the campmate network an ego was roughly 37-51x (point ~44x) more likely to name an alter who named them; (3) cooperator assortment - cooperators clustered with cooperators, an association extending out to two degrees of separation in gift networks; plus transitivity and geographic decay. The output was a camp continually re-composed of preferred, reciprocating, similarly-cooperative partners.
parameters.modern_default: Where modern matching exists (dating apps, professional networks, recommender feeds), the optimization target is engagement, novelty, or proximity-of-the-moment, not durable mutual reciprocity, demonstrated cooperativeness, or transitive trust within a personally-known group.
parameters.gap_statement: The EEA delivered a continuous, agency-rich sorting process that filtered one's immediate social world toward reciprocating, cooperative, vouched-for partners. The modern environment inverts this: the explicit matching systems that do exist optimize for engagement/novelty rather than reciprocity and demonstrated cooperation. The result is reduced control over WHO populates one's social field, weaker assortment on actual cooperativeness, and loss of the transitive-reputation signal that let ancestral humans cluster with trustworthy reciprocators out to two degrees. The mismatch is a broken selection rule: the inputs the ancestral algorithm ran on (mutual choice, observed reciprocity, cooperator reputation) are no longer the primary determinants of who one lives and works among.

parameters.name: Relationship longevity & maintenance (durable dyads; maintenance institutions like hxaro conserve bonds across distance)
parameters.eea_baseline: In ancestral foraging life the load-bearing social unit was the durable, reciprocal DYAD, not the group. Groups continuously reshuffled (entire camps shifted location every 4 to 8 weeks, with most campmates changing from one survey wave to the next). Among the Ju/'hoansi, hxaro was a formal delayed-reciprocity gift-partnership system with ties passed down across generations (ext 2272), spanning dispersed bands up to ~200 km apart; the average person spent 4.4 months a year living with hxaro partners (ext 752). Trivers's conditions for the evolution of reciprocal altruism describe exactly this regime: a long lifetime, low dispersal, and repeated interaction with the same small set of individuals, so that an investment in a specific partner reliably paid back over time.

eea_value._note: The 200 km hxaro range and about 15 partners per adult come from Wiessner & Huang 2022 (ext 752; Ju/'hoansi, 1974). Partnerships passed down across generations: Wiessner & Huang 2022 (ext 2272). For turnover: no number is used; see campmate_turnover_status. Camps shift every ~4-8 weeks (Smith et al. 2018, core work 116).

parameters.modern_default: The modern environment inverts the ancestral pattern: it supplies stable GROUP labels (a workplace, a school cohort, a social-media feed, a city) while the dyads inside them are shallow and disposable, and there is no institutional equivalent of hxaro that conserves a specific bond once physical proximity ends. When two people stop sharing a context, the relationship is simply allowed to decay; nothing structurally obligates either party to keep servicing it. Dunbar proposes that friendships require recurring face-to-face contact to avoid sliding down through the network layers and eventually dropping out of the personal network entirely, and that online media at best slows that decay rather than preventing it (ext 509). Sutcliffe and colleagues propose that trust is a function of the time invested in a relationship, and that the costs of maintaining a relationship (most obviously, time) are roughly linear with the number of relationships (ext 503, 505).
parameters.gap_statement: The specific missing piece is a maintenance institution: the EEA had hxaro-type structures (formalized, inheritable, distance-spanning, long-term delayed reciprocity) that actively preserved a named dyad, whereas modernity has no hxaro-equivalent and instead relies on shared proximity/context as the only glue. When that proximity ends (job change, move, leaving school), the bond is not migrated to an institution that keeps it alive; it decays. The result is many stable-looking memberships sitting on top of disposable, shallow ties.
parameters.resolution_unit: The durable, spatially-dispersed reciprocal DYAD plus the maintenance institutions that conserve it across distance and time, i.e., a specific named partner whose bond is actively serviced (face-to-face when possible, and via hxaro-type delayed-reciprocity exchange when apart) so the relationship persists and survives the reshuffling of any particular group. The resolution requires migrating a bond to an institution that keeps it alive once proximity ends, not merely accumulating more low-investment ties.
parameters.confidence_note: Grade: tested once. Hxaro range and partner count: Wiessner & Huang 2022 (ext 752), Ju/'hoansi only. Camps move every 4 to 8 weeks (Smith et al. 2018, ext 604, Hadza), and no turnover number is used (see EEA-SOC-05). Modern side: Dunbar proposes that friendships decay without face-to-face meetings and that social media only slow the decay (Dunbar 2016, ext 509, 510; cross-sectional data). In the model of Sutcliffe et al. 2012, the time cost of keeping relationships grows in line with their number, and trust grows with time invested (ext 503, 505; theoretical). Trivers argues that reciprocity is favoured by a long lifetime, low dispersal and repeated interaction with the same few individuals (Trivers 1971, ext 479).

parameters.name: Novel-stranger frequency
parameters.eea_baseline: Social cognition operated over a bounded pool: a personally-known reference network capped near the ~150 Dunbar ceiling, nested in ~5/15/50/150 layers of decreasing intimacy. Within that architecture almost every face encountered was already known, placed, and reputationally tracked. A genuinely novel stranger, an individual who could not be located anywhere in one's known network or in the known networks of one's allies, was therefore a comparatively rare event. Because the bounded pool had no slot for such a person, novelty itself was diagnostic: a never-before-seen individual could not be vouched for, had no shared reputational history, and could not be assumed to be bound by the local web of reciprocity and norm enforcement. Encounters with unplaceable strangers were thus both infrequent and highly salient, and the threat-management system (M1) treated unfamiliarity as a plausible danger cue to be resolved (placed, vouched-for, or avoided) rather than as a routine background condition. This is an inference from the bounded-pool architecture plus M1, not a directly measured ancestral rate.
parameters.modern_default: The M1 machinery still treats unplaceable others as potential threats.
parameters.gap_statement: The delta is one of base rate and resolvability. Ancestrally, novel strangers were rare, salient, and resolvable (place them in the known web, or treat unfamiliarity as an actionable threat signal); modernity inverts this to constant, non-diagnostic, unresolvable novelty. The threat-management system inherited from the rare-stranger regime cannot down-regulate to the new base rate: it either over-fires (chronic low-grade vigilance, stranger-directed wariness in crowds and online) or, where it habituates, leaves people transacting with a stream of others who carry none of the reputational accountability the system implicitly assumes. The conserved unit being eroded is not the count of strangers but the durable, reputationally-tracked dyad against which any new face used to be evaluated; once almost everyone is a stranger, the bounded-pool premise that made novelty meaningful no longer holds.
parameters.resolution_unit: The durable, reputationally-tracked reciprocal dyad: ancestrally every new face was evaluated against a finite web of known, vouched-for relationships, and it was that web of bonds - not the count of strangers per se - that gave novelty its diagnostic and protective meaning. The mismatch resolves only insofar as new encounters can be anchored back into durable, accountable relationships rather than left as anonymous one-off contacts.
parameters.confidence_note: Grade: argued, not yet tested. No study measures how often ancestral humans met strangers. The premise is a bounded pool of personally known people in nested layers of about 5, 12, 35 and 150 (Dunbar 1998, ext 490), with a limit, argued by Dunbar 1992 (ext 485), on how many relationships a person can monitor at once. For the stranger-as-threat side: in chimpanzees, attacks from conspecifics, including lethal raids by males from neighbouring groups, are major sources of mortality (Hrdy 2009, ext 383), and across 18 communities most killings were by males and of members of other communities (Wilson et al. 2014, ext 671). This is animal evidence. Ambush killing between groups is documented in several nomadic forager societies, and how often it happened is disputed (Wrangham & Glowacki 2012, ext 672; Bowles 2009, ext 673). Infants show wariness toward an approaching stranger in lab studies (Waters et al. 1975, ext 676). In 21 mobile forager bands most recorded killings were homicides, a few were feuds and a minority were war (Fry & Söderberg 2013, ext 674), and Tomasello describes cooperation with in-group strangers (Tomasello 2014, ext 238, 250). Bowlby's claim that strangers are an innate fear cue (ext 574) comes from a book that was not read directly and is not linked as evidence.

parameters.name: Behavioral observability / reputation visibility
parameters.eea_baseline: In a band/camp embedded in a personally-known reference group, a person's relevant behavior was directly observable by, or transmitted through gossip to, people who knew them by name and knew their history. Reputation was a shared, continuously-updated, distributed record: as Boehm puts it, "the band keeps a dossier on every individual, noting positive and negative points." Where campmates differed, they knew it: asked one by one in 12 Hadza camps, they agreed more on who hunts best (r 0.23) and a little more on who works hardest (r 0.08). They barely agreed on who shares the most food, who tells the fewest lies and who has the best heart (ext 2795). Project position (21 Nov 2026): anyone still in camp shared and was honest enough to be kept there, so on those points there was little left to rank, and such labels sort strangers more than campmates. The study's authors read the low agreement as moral behaviour that changes across time and situations to fit local circumstances (ext 2796). Observability had teeth: those who deviated (theft, deception, stinginess, free-riding) were subject to gossip, ridicule, ostracism, and ultimately exclusion, and everyone knew this monitoring was constant, so it functioned as a deterrent and most foragers tried to exert self-control accordingly. Tomasello argues that because foraging was obligately collaborative, individuals had to evaluate partners and track how they themselves were being evaluated (ext 239). The net result: visibility was embodied, hard to fake over time, attached to a single durable identity, and backed by real consequences.
parameters.modern_default: The visibility that does exist is mediated, curated, and quantitatively inflated. On average, UK respondents considered only 27.6% of their Facebook friends genuine close friends (with a strong modal value between 0 and 10%), so networks are padded with weakly-accountable acquaintances rather than people tracking one's actual conduct. Mediated contact cannot substitute for the embodied, face-to-face observation the bonding/reputation system evolved for: Dunbar proposes that without periodic in-person contact, ties decay through the network layers into mere acquaintance, and that social media may slow this decay (ext 509). Visibility is now selectively self-presented (gameable), fragmented across multiple personas and contexts, and policed (if at all) by distant institutions or algorithms rather than by named peers with whom one shares a future. Reputation is either absent (anonymity), sortable away (exit/blocking, fresh accounts), or captured by platform metrics.
parameters.gap_statement: The ancestral environment delivered embodied, hard-to-fake, single-identity behavioral observability inside a reference group whose members knew one's history and held real enforcement power. The modern environment delivers visibility that is mediated, curated, gameable, fragmented across exitable contexts, padded with non-accountable weak ties, and largely stripped of peer-enforced consequences. The reputation-tracking machinery (M11) and status-position monitoring (M5) evolved to run on dense, durable, accountable observation now operate on thin, performative, low-accountability signals, producing both reputational impunity for defection among strangers and chronic exposure of curated personas to vast unfamiliar audiences with no reciprocal knowledge of the person behind them.
parameters.confidence_note: Grade: argued, not yet tested. Forager bands track reputation through gossip, ridicule and ostracism (Boehm 1999, ext 373, 375), and Tomasello argues that partners evaluate each other (Tomasello 2014, ext 239). The threat of gossip made people more generous in experiments (Feinberg et al. 2012, ext 719), and in 15 small-scale communities shame tracked how much the community would devalue an act (Sznycer et al. 2018, ext 722). Modern side: respondents counted only 27.6% of their Facebook friends as genuine (Dunbar 2016, ext 508), and Dunbar proposes that ties decay without face-to-face meetings (ext 509; cross-sectional data). Two meta-analyses found no evidence that artificial surveillance cues, such as images of watching eyes, raise generosity (Northover et al. 2017, ext 829). No study compares ancestral and modern observability directly. The comparison is the framework's reading.

evidence.author_quote: In the hypothesis of Tomasello et al. (2012), obligate collaborative foraging became an evolutionarily stable strategy for early humans because of two interrelated processes: interdependence and social selection. The first and most basic point is that humans began a lifestyle in which individuals could not procure their daily sustenance alone but instead were interdependent with others in their foraging activities - which meant that individuals needed to develop the skills and motivations to forage collaboratively or else starve. There was thus direct and immediate selective pressure for skills and motivations for joint collaborative activity (joint intentionality). The second point is that as a natural outcome of this interdependence, individuals began to make evaluative judgments about others as potential collaborative partners: they began to be socially selective, since choosing a poor partner meant less food. Cheaters and laggards were thus selected against, and bullies lost their power to bully.

parameters.name: Leadership and dominance (no rulers; prestige; exit available)
parameters.eea_baseline: Mobile hunter-gatherer bands had no rulers. Decisions that affected the group were reached by discussion toward consensus. Influence came from prestige. Anyone who tried to dominate was mocked, shunned or expelled, and in extreme cases killed. People could also leave a camp for another one, and that option checked anyone who tried to take control.
parameters.modern_default: Rulers are chosen at state scale. The polity is in practice impossible to leave.
parameters.gap_statement: The forager checks on dominance (ridicule, shunning, walking away, a voice in a face-to-face decision) have no reach over rulers. One person's say shrinks from a share of a camp consensus to one vote.
parameters.confidence_note: Grade, rubric v2 (22 Nov 2026): tested many times for mobile foragers. Mobile foragers suppress would-be dominants across the ethnographic record (Boehm 1993, ext 688), and among egalitarian hunter-gatherers leadership depends on individual ability and demonstrated success in activities the group values (Garfield, von Rueden and Hagen 2019, ext 689); main weakness: the ethnographies differ in method and date. Singh and Glowacki 2022 (ext 756) review 34 regions and argue that sedentary, unequal non-agricultural societies also existed through the Late Pleistocene; their data are mostly sedentary Holocene societies, and they do not dispute the description of mobile foragers. The baseline describes mobile, immediate-return foragers (Woodburn 1982, ext 677). Mbendjele BaYaka mock men who hunt a lot and in effect exiled one persistent hunter; braggarts are teased, avoided and if they persist exiled (Lewis 2014, ext 848). Tsimane fishing-trip organisers rotate across households and take no more fish than others (von Rueden et al. 2014, ext 1038). Ju/'hoansi kept social, gender and political equality for decades after cash created large wealth gaps (Wiessner and Huang 2022, ext 1034). Wealth inequality itself: EEA-SOC-14.

parameters.name: Food shared and eaten in company
parameters.eea_baseline: A review of 45 small-scale groups reports food transfers beyond the household throughout, and in all 10 groups where it was checked big game reached more families than small game. Among the Hadza of Tanzania at least 90% of the meat of large animals left the hunter's household. Among the Aka of the Congo a cook and her children ate about 20% of the stew she made, about 75% of the stew a woman ate came from other women's pots, serving was done in plain view, and the men usually ate together at the men's shelter. Among the Ju/'hoansi of Botswana each family ate the evening meal at its own fire and people then gathered at shared fires. Among the Great Andamanese a pig brought home whole was roasted at a public cooking place and each family ate at its own hut. Batek camps in Malaysia, about 34 people, shared food at once, stored none and ate almost nothing out of camp. Hadza men ate on the foray, out of camp, about 90 percent of what they are estimated to spend in a day, most of it honey (ext 3162). No record shows a whole camp eating as one table every day. Sharing with the whole band was the exception and went with bands under 40 to 50 people.
parameters.modern_default: In the United States 26% of adults ate every meal of the previous day alone in 2023, more than half again above the 2003 level; among people living alone it was about 70%.
